the watchdog now lives outside the registry it watches: X:\Claude\registry-heartbeat.py runs hourly from the native Windows task claude-registry-heartbeat, registered by X:\Claude\register-registry-heartbeat-task.ps1 at 20 past the hour and verified running with LastTaskResult 0 at 00:55 on 2026-09-05. It checks the task-folder count under C:\Users\Kane\.claude\scheduled-tasks, parses the live registry, requires a firing inside 30 hours, and requires the backup chain to be under 48 hours old and to hold a full roster. Failure raises four channels: a Windows toast, X:\Claude\REGISTRY-HEARTBEAT-ALERT.md, CLAUDE-ROUTINES-STOPPED.txt on the desktop, and a line in X:\OPEN-LOOPS.md that the [loops] hook prints at every session start; --test-alert fired all four and the first healthy run withdrew them, restoring OPEN-LOOPS.md byte for byte. routine-health-watch gained a bullet reading registry-heartbeat-state.json, so a dead heartbeat is itself detected.
